Unit_Conversions_Notes: pH and Temperature_C: mean of 47 main-channel supplement samples for this season (Horgby-et-al-Supplementary-data.xlsx, 'Streamwater data' sheet; season parsed from ID prefix). Discharge: paper's own seasonal mainstem average (Results 3.1, n=46 sampling sites this season per Table 2). CO2_flux: paper's own areal CO2 evasion flux average across the stream network (Results 3.5/Table 5) = 21.7 umol C/m2/s x 12 x 86400/1e6 = 22.499 gC/m2/d (from the Ulseth et al. 2019 gas-transfer-velocity model, not recomputed here). External_Pathway = CO2_flux (100%): Results 3.4's isotope mixing model partitions the ENTIRE streamwater CO2 source between soil respiration (50% this season) and carbonate mineral weathering (remainder) -- both delivered via groundwater from outside the stream, so both count as External under this pipeline's definition (correcting an earlier version of this recipe that mislabeled the carbonate-weathering share as 'Internal'). Internal_Pathway UPDATED (user instruction): the Discussion (p.1972) separately tests genuine in-stream ecosystem respiration via a DOC/d13C-DIC mass-balance sensitivity check and concludes it 'contributed only marginally' (DOC-fueled respiration could explain at most ~0.14 permil of isotopic enrichment, requiring an implausible 86.4% DOC increase to fully explain the observed shift), 'in general agreement' with results from Hotchkiss et al. (2015)'s continental-scale synthesis of U.S. streams -- but the paper itself never converts this into a flux value. Per user instruction, Internal_Pathway is instead estimated by log-linear interpolation (on log10 discharge) of Hotchkiss et al. (2015)'s discharge-vs-internal(ecosystem-respiration)-CO2-flux relationship (table digitized in C:/Dissertation/03_Scripts/Streams/figures/meta analysis.R), evaluated at this season's mean discharge (Q=0.14 m3/s): internal = 1.249 gC/m2/d. This is a literature-derived proxy, NOT a value reported by Horgby et al. themselves, and is NOT subtracted from External_Pathway (which remains Horgby's own isotope-based 100% partition per Results 3.4) -- Internal+External therefore exceeds CO2_flux by this proxy amount, flagged here rather than mass-balance-closed.
Source: Table 2 (sampling n) + supplement xlsx (pH) + Results 3.1 (discharge) + Results 3.5/Table 5 (CO2 evasion flux) + Results 3.4 (source apportionment %) + Discussion p.1972 (in-stream respiration sensitivity check), Horgby et al. 2019

Unit_Conversions_Notes: Discharge = 2.09 m3/s, stream flow rate at the most downstream site during the May 2019 field campaign (Results 3.1) -- the reach-scale carbon budget below was measured during this campaign; longer-term annual mean at the gauging station is 2.41 m3/s (2001-2007, Site description). pH ~8.50 (Methods 2.2, approximate value stated for context on indirect CO2 calculation accuracy). Temperature_C NOT REPORTED: stream temperature was measured in the field (Methods 2.2) but no numeric summary value is given anywhere in the accessible text. CO2_flux = stream CO2 evasion rate FCO2air (Fick's Law, calibrated 222Rn gas-transfer velocity; Results 3.4/Fig. 6b), reach-averaged. Internal_Pathway = net internal CO2 production FCO2m (reach-scale dissolved O2 mass balance, RQ=0.85 per Song et al. 2018; Results 3.3/Fig. 5d) -- independently modeled, NOT recomputed via this pipeline's own RQ=1.0 formula (paper uses its own O2 mass-balance + RQ=0.85, different methodology than the GPP/ER time-series approach used elsewhere in this meta-analysis). External_Pathway = terrestrial CO2 input FCO2gw (222Rn/water mass balance x groundwater CO2 concentration; Results 3.2/Fig. 5c-d) -- also independently modeled. CO2_flux is NOT the residual of Internal+External here (unlike most papers in this pipeline): the paper's own carbon budget (Fig. 6a, Results 3.4) shows carbonate buffering removes 4.12 +/- 1.98 gC/m2/d from the volatile CO2 pool (precipitating calcite, calcite saturation index 1.03 +/- 0.15) before evasion, and a further 1.86 +/- 0.56 gC/m2/d is exported downstream as dissolved CO2 rather than evaded within this reach -- both are why Internal+External (5.66) substantially exceeds the measured local evasion rate (1.27).
